Training objectives (what officers should know or be able to do after the training)
Target audience (e.g. new frontline officers, IT compliance engineers, case workers)
Preferred output format (slide deck / eLearning module / written guide / facilitator guide)
Approximate length or duration target
instructions: Read the source policy documents and identify the content relevant to the training objectives.
Map the content to a learning structure: key concepts, step-by-step procedures, common scenarios, and assessments.
Draft the training content for each section in language appropriate to the target audience — plain and direct for frontline officers, technically precise for IT engineers.
For slide decks: create a structured slide outline with one key message per slide, supported by concise bullet points and suggested visuals or diagrams.
For written guides: use numbered steps for procedures, callout boxes for important rules or warnings, and examples to illustrate abstract concepts.
Include a short knowledge check or quiz at the end of each module with 3–5 questions.
Output the draft training material in the requested format using the appropriate tool (Canva for visuals, Articulate/Rise for eLearning, Word/Google Docs for written guides).
toolsAllowed: Canva (SaaS); Articulate 360 / Rise (SaaS eLearning authoring); Notion (SaaS); publicly available policy documents (agency websites); Claude / GPT-4 API (SaaS LLM); Gamma.app (SaaS presentation AI)
outputFormat: Training material in the specified format: slide deck (PowerPoint / Canva), eLearning module (Articulate/Rise export), or written guide (PDF/Word) — with knowledge check questions appended, and a facilitator notes section if the format is instructor-led.
constraintsList: All training content must be reviewed and approved by the owning policy or HR team before use in officer training.
Do not include information from restricted or confidential policy documents without appropriate clearance.
Knowledge check questions must be validated by a subject matter expert to ensure accuracy.
failureHandling: If the source policy documents are insufficient to cover the training objectives, flag the content gap and request additional reference materials. If the eLearning authoring tool is unavailable, fall back to a written guide format.
skillExamples: Input: IM8 data governance policy, training objective: new IT officers understand data classification requirements, target: 30-minute eLearning module. Output: 6-section eLearning module covering classification levels, handling requirements, and breach procedures — with 5-question knowledge check and facilitator guide.

name: FAQ Generation from Policies
description: Create frequently asked questions content from government policies for citizens — enabling faster publication of accessible citizen resources.
targetJobRoles: Digital Ambassadors; Frontline Service Officers; Communications Officers
dependencies: Policy documents; FAQ template
saasDependencies: Publicly published government policy documents (e.g. cpf.gov.sg, hdb.gov.sg, moh.gov.sg); SaaS LLM API (Claude / GPT-4); Notion / Confluence (SaaS output); isomer.gov.sg CMS (open-source Singapore Gov CMS)
implementabilityNote: All input documents are publicly available on government websites. FAQ generation is a pure LLM task on public text. Output goes to standard SaaS or Isomer (open-source gov CMS). Easiest skill to implement on this entire list — zero internal systems needed.
whenToUse: When a digital ambassador, frontline service officer, or communications officer needs to create FAQ content for a government website, service portal, or citizen communications from a policy document — without drafting from scratch.
inputs: Source policy document or policy web page URL (e.g. CPF.gov.sg, HDB.gov.sg, MOH.gov.sg)
Target audience (e.g. general public, businesses, elderly citizens)
Number of FAQs to generate (or 'as many as needed')
Tone (formal / conversational)
Existing FAQ list (optional, for deduplication and gap-filling)
instructions: Load the source policy document or fetch the policy web page content.
Read the policy and identify the most likely questions a citizen would have — focus on eligibility, entitlements, application process, timelines, exceptions, and contact points.
If an existing FAQ list is provided, identify gaps and avoid duplicating covered questions.

Draft each FAQ in question-and-answer format: question phrased in natural citizen language ('How do I...?', 'Am I eligible...?', 'What happens if...?'); answer concise and direct (2–4 sentences) in plain language appropriate to the target audience.
Group FAQs by logical theme (e.g. Eligibility, Application Process, Payment, Appeals).
Apply a readability check to confirm answers are at an appropriate reading level.
Output the FAQ set, organised by theme, ready for review and publication.
toolsAllowed: Publicly published government policy documents (e.g. cpf.gov.sg, hdb.gov.sg, moh.gov.sg); SaaS LLM API (Claude / GPT-4); Notion / Confluence (SaaS output); isomer.gov.sg CMS (open-source Singapore Gov CMS)
outputFormat: FAQ document (Word, Notion page, or CMS-ready format) with FAQs organised by theme, each with a clearly worded question and a plain language answer of 2–4 sentences — ready for review and publication on the agency website or service portal.
constraintsList: All FAQ content must be reviewed and approved by the owning policy or communications team before publication.
Do not create FAQs that involve legal advice or that commit the government to specific interpretations of law — flag these for legal review.
Ensure all answers are accurate as of the policy version used; note the policy version and date in the document footer.
failureHandling: If the source policy document is unclear or contradictory on a point, draft the FAQ with a placeholder note flagging the ambiguity for the policy team to resolve. If the policy web page cannot be fetched, request the user to provide the text directly.
skillExamples: Input: CPF Retirement Sum Scheme policy page, general public audience, conversational tone, 15 FAQs. Output: 15 FAQs in 4 themes (What is the Retirement Sum Scheme, Eligibility, How to Apply, Receiving Payouts) — reviewed by CPF Board communications team before publication on CPF.gov.sg.
